campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda listed routine items like bill payments and monthly financial reports, alongside a proclamation for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a donation of blackout shades for the Heritage Theatre, and an $8.5 million state grant application for park development. The agenda also included staff compensation resolutions, a City Manager salary adjustment, and advisory committee appointments.
keyTopics: Proclamation recognizing October 2026 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, honoring El Camino Health
Resolution to apply for an $8,500,000 state grant through the Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program
Acceptance of a donated $16,680 motorized blackout shades for the Heritage Theatre auditorium
Resolutions amending compensation and working conditions for unrepresented Confidential, Classified Management, and Unclassified Management employees, plus a City Manager salary adjustment
Appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Civic Improvement Commission

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026 agenda includes routine items like meeting minutes, check registers, and a Treasurer's report, alongside several notable decisions: a $2.5 million budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation, a proposal for new parking restrictions on Chester Avenue, and a major discussion on whether to switch the city's long-term law enforcement provider to the Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department. The agenda also lists a review of animal care service providers and a public hearing on annual updates to the City Code.
keyTopics: Budget amendment of $2,500,000 for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project
Proposed No Parking Anytime zone on both sides of Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Discussion and potential decision on switching long-term law enforcement services to the Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of regional animal care providers, including whether to continue with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Public hearing on 2026 annual City Code updates covering appeals scheduling and City Commissioner qualifications

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026 included a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a VTA board appointment, a temporary moratorium on certain detention/custodial facility applications, and appointments to several city commissions. The agenda also listed a legal services contract amendment and a review of the upcoming council calendar and Housing Element implementation schedule.
keyTopics: Resolution authorizing Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant Basic Agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan D. Weinberg to the VTA Board for an additional two years
Interim Urgency Ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on applications for detention or custodial facilities and custodial-processing facilities
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment No. 1 to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, updating fees to a $21,500 monthly retainer plus a $385 hourly rate

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026 agenda covers routine business, including approval of prior meeting minutes, accounts payable, and payroll reports. It also includes a bid issue with a tree services contractor, an amendment to an existing agreement, updates to the Finance Commission's work plan, a proposed change to the Town's purchasing policy, and a financial report covering July 2026.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an existing Town agreement
Finance Commission's updated 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 7, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is the agenda for San José's Rules and Open Government Committee meeting, which mainly handles scheduling for upcoming City Council meetings. The October 13 meeting was cancelled, and the agenda lists plans to review and build the October 20 draft agenda, along with routine reports and a couple of specific items proposed for future Council consideration.
keyTopics: October 13, 2026 Council meeting cancelled
Building the October 20, 2026 draft agenda, including adding items and assigning time-certain slots
A joint special meeting between the City of San José and Santa Clara Valley Water District
A proposed proclamation and flag-raising event for Taiwan Retrocession Day, sponsored by Council District 5
A proposed item on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: This Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee agenda covers the city's draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. The meeting included options for the public to join virtually or by phone to comment on these items.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026 includes recognitions for Little League All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week, along with routine approvals of minutes, claims, and contract amendments. The agenda also lists public hearings on water conservation rules for nonfunctional turf, a possible service worker retention ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Public hearing and proposed ordinance to prohibit potable water use for irrigating nonfunctional turf, implementing state law AB 1572 (listed as CEQA-exempt under Guidelines Section 15307)
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation

Amendment to a contract with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill, increasing the not-to-exceed amount to $385,000 and extending it through October 2028
Resolution to increase the salary for the Public Safety Communications Manager classification

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda includes a closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue, along with routine consent items like meeting minutes and treasurer's reports. Notable items include a property exchange agreement for the Finch property valued at $11.8 million, a public hearing on conduit financing for The RISE development, and a public information session on soil contamination remediation at The RISE.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of the Community Development Department (Planning, Building, Housing, and Code Enforcement Divisions)
Approval of a resolution increasing employer PEMHCA medical insurance contributions for retired annuitants hired before August 2004
Approval of an Exchange Agreement for the Finch Property at a negotiated purchase price of $11.8 million
Public information session on approved soil contamination remediation plan at The Rise, plus a TEFRA public hearing on conduit financing for the project

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council and Stadium Authority Board have a joint agenda that includes proclamations, routine consent items, and several substantive policy discussions. Key topics on the agenda include pedestrian access restrictions near Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways, data center development policy, and multiple councilmember requests related to data centers and resident parking issues near the stadium.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action on pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Staff presentation on a comprehensive approach to updating city policies on new data center development, including water usage and grid support
Councilmember Hardy's request for a staff update on entitlement and power allocation processes for data centers, with a possible moratorium on standalone data centers
Councilmember Hardy's proposal to prohibit the city from entering non-disclosure agreements with standalone data centers

Councilmember Park's requests regarding resident parking near apartment complexes, compensation for vehicles ticketed/towed during stadium events, and parking requirements for affordable housing projects

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council's September 15, 2026 agenda listed a review of the city's Community Development Block Grant funding plan for 2025, a presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program, and an assessment of the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also included actions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including the sale and issuance of refunding bonds.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution and bond actions for the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: Palo Alto's Climate Action and Sustainability Committee published an agenda for its October 2, 2026 meeting that includes staff and committee member comments, plus an update on long duration resiliency for the electric system. The agenda notes this electric system item is categorized as 'Not a Project' under CEQA.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency, with a staff presentation
CEQA determination for the resiliency item listed as 'Not a Project'
Staff comments
Committee member comments and announcements
